author: JuanDiablo1980
title: Money Pit, not fun anymore
content:
I have been playing this game for a long time. With that said, I understand the need for the developer to create some sort of revenue; however, throughout the years and especially lately, you can’t pass more than one level without needing some power-up or extra coins. I thought it was just me exaggerating, so I recorded myself playing for a few days. On average (and this is taking my time to evaluate possible moves), I’d be required to use either a power-up (Anvils or Boxing Gloves) or extra coins eight  out of every 10 games, or I would lose whatever progress I have as well as other “Perks” or supposed assistance you get if you maintain a “No losing streak.” 
And without those, forget about passing levels at all. 
There are no ways of obtaining free power-ups or coins like they used to do by watching an ad.  
The game or its developers got money-hungry as the platform grew, and now it’s just a money pit if you want to actually play more than one level with the five free lives you get as a standard player. If you invest some of your hard-earned money into it, then the game gets worse and worse, forcing you to use up everything you purchased (And real quick) to retain the “Perks” you earned.  
I’ve read other reviews, and they all claim the same, and the developers’ response is that the game is randomly generated. 
But I’m a software developer by trade and have recorded over 100 levels played, and there is no way that the randomness they talk about is not twisted to make you lose by one move (every six to nine games) on average.  
Bottom line, it’s NOT a fun game anymore, and I’d recommend you look elsewhere for something entertaining.

author: AprilInHB
title: Champions League is ruining the fun
content:
I've been playing this for several years and thought I was getting the hang of it. I could play a few levels each day and then walk away. Then they began adding multiple side challenges. If I tackled those it was a good way to bank extra coins and boosters. Then this Champions League showed up last month. It quickly became clear that they made this a much more difficult level of play that I never signed up for and was stuck playing for about 25 days. I hated it and was so happy when the Champions League was finished a couple days ago. 

In this "League" all of the levels have a ridiculously low number of moves available and that there was no way to complete many of them without using up my boosters and coins needed to give me the 5 "extra" moves (moves that they subtracted from the level in order to drain your saved coins). Of course this means you go broke faster and can't "buy" more boosters without shelling out real money. 

Today the Champions League reappeared and once again you can't opt out of joining and it's the same annoying ordeal: fewer moves with fewer tile matches causing you to again start using up the boosters and coins you may have just won, thus repeating the shakedown. Once my coins run out it's going to be time to move on to a new game. The fun vanishes quickly when the game feels like a chore you must rush through or lose any chance at continuing game play. Yes, you can play without boosters or coins as the Dev has commented on other reviews. That's ignoring the fact your users are saying it isn't fun repeating the same level over and over until the game eventually relents and gives you enough matching tiles to create in-game boosts - only to repeat this on the next level. Listen to your reviewers or you'll lose previously happy players.

author: LilyPotter130
title: A frustrating waste of time
content:
I’ve written several reviews carefully explaining the issues, and they’ve been either removed or hidden. This is the last one I will waste my time writing.

At the beginning, this game is fun and addictive. At the higher levels, it becomes increasingly more bug-ridden, with ads malfunctioning and causing you to lose progress. And speaking of ads, most of them are at least 45 seconds long, and they require multiple taps to progress through the ad. Several of them take more than a minute, and it’s really not worth it after awhile. There are a few ads that are downright violent, and there was one that was sexual and OBSCENE. That is not only inappropriate, it’s unacceptable for a game that is approved for all ages.

I don’t care what the developers say; this game is NOT fair. The algorithms are horribly bad, and they’re programmed against the player. It’s impossible to strategize, when the odds are against you. You simply end up tapping your screen endlessly and uselessly for days on one level, while you wait for the win. If you don’t believe me, play for awhile and you’ll find out for yourself. And speaking of the developers, whenever anyone writes a negative review, they offer a pathetic “copy-paste” response, and they NEVER address the problems.

I don’t know about anyone else, but I play games to unwind and relax. Over time, I’ve come to realize that this game is the antithesis of fun and relaxing. It’s frustrating beyond belief to be trapped on levels for days on end, and no amount of strategizing or skill will fix that.

content: This game is really cool. Nice graphics. But it cheats. When you’re leading in a tourney and trying to stretch your lead it’ll give you bad draws with the blocks. It’ll be mathematically impossible unless you purchase power ups. I understand letting others catch up. But if you make us wait almost a half hour to play don’t cheat us. That’s petty. They got a paywall. It’s like a rigged slot machine. After like 10 attempts they make it easier then let you roll through with easier ones, then it plateaus, making it impossible. All to make YOU feel like a loser and pay more. The gaming commission should regulate this stuff. I waited hours to keep retrying. They stole part of life waiting for them to cheat me out of enjoyment. I’m far too poor to pay. Nice game otherwise. If it wasn’t for them actively cheating I would’ve gave it 5 stars. I screenshot this as my last review was erased. If you see this then know this is an honest review.

author: bjpruitt
title: Progress toward frustration
content: I quickly got addicted to this game and played it whenever I could get the needed lives. The first few hundred levels were a great mix of challenging and occasional easy ones, but once I got to level 1000 it turned so frustrating. I worked my way to the top level finally, almost quitting several times because it was so frustrating. Now that I'm at the championship level, I'm contemplating quitting again. At this advanced level, rather than reward the advanced players, they have taken away rewards and made the puzzles not only harder, but just boring recycles of previous levels. Unless the developers do some changes and start to reward advanced players, they will lose me as a player.

author: Poggle757
title: Still love this game even tho…
content: Toon blast is still one of the best running games I’ve played. Never freezes…EVER! They continue to add levels and side challenges, love the tournament on the weekend, have an awesome team! I am a little disappointed that the coin prizes have been lowering and instead of winning coins for the team chest all of a sudden one day you were given an hour of endless life instead without any kind of warning 😧 I do love Toon Blast, the work you have put into this game has greatly paid off, the game runs so smoothly and quickly makes the game play soooo much more enjoyable! And I will say I thought it was a nice addition to give us the option to watch a video for 3 more moves! Keep up the good work. Thank you so much

author: (*Maggie*)
title: Fun but BEWARE
content: This is a fun game but they punish you for being too good at it, and then you can just kiss your actual money goodbye, trying to keep your power-ups. The higher you get, the less moves they give you to complete levels. In certain leagues, you will be number 5 in your league, but on your friend’s phone you’re number one and they’re congratulating you on winnings that you’re never going to see. Also, where your friend will only need to pass 400 levels to earn a Wild Card, you will have to pass 500, and I’m guessing the scammers hope you never confer and figure that out. What’s more, I was double-charged for coin packages on my credit card which I had to get refunded. If the levels and moves were equal for everyone, I’d keep playing, but it just sets you up to fail and pay real money, the higher you go. Oh! And once you’ve paid real money for anything, they won’t give you the option to watch an ad to get more moves. Total con!

author: Stevie32101234
title: Review
content:
I have playing for years and am now at the top of the score board. I have found the difficulty has increased as I move up the board. At one time, I could watch ads to get extra moves if I used up all the moves I had. This was taken away and when I contacted the game, I was told that is what they do. I have to use coins to get extra lives and the only way to gain coins is when my team wins the weekend competition. I then get 500 coins which I can use on five games.
It seems the changes being made to the game are to primarily being made to force people to spend money to get coins. Since the several other game changes, I have seen less people playing on our team and playing in the weekend competitions. I don’t enjoy playing as much, but I play to support my teammates.

author: dorianh49
title: The Devs delved too greedily and too deep
content:
I’ve been playing the game for several years now and have become pretty good at it. I’ve noticed definite patterns: the direction of the arrows is NOT random; the dev’s algorithm usually sets arrows in certain columns to point in the least optimal position for the player to beat the level. I’ll need just one arrow to point downwards, but all 8-10 in the same column will face sideways. Every. Time. That is NOT random.

I’ve also noticed that, after making a purchase, the levels become easier for a while. It seems that the devs want you to associate $$ with winning. Not uncommon, and I had gotten good enough to amass over 20,000 coins and tons of boosts without breaking the bank; most were won from events and missions.

A few months ago, however, the devs seemingly ramped up the difficulty of the game to an insane level while also making inexpensive special packs rarer. There’s usually a $3 and $5 pack available every weekend, but one especially difficult weekend, the cheapest available “special” pack was $50. Yes, $50. The greed is just so in your face.

Every one of my team members complained about the sudden increase of difficulty, and from the low scores of our weekly competition, it appears that everyone is on the same struggle bus.

My 20,000 coins and plentiful boosts have dwindled over the last few months and were finally depleted this morning. It’s just not fun anymore. So, it’s time to delete the game. I recommend avoiding Toon Blast and anything by Peak Games unless you like getting your heart broken.

author: galbelle
title: First game played and deleting
content: This is the first game I ever installed after seeing ads for it in a card game. So first game of this type. I am older and not used to playing this type of game. At first it was fun to move up levels try strategies to get past them, etc. Then the levels got harder and harder and I  would get stuck on one for weeks, this is no longer fun but frustrating. It is making me anxious. After being stuck in a level in the high 100s for weeks ,I beat it by  using all of my boosters I had saved, and will delete it. I am playing other games that at least strategy and persistence pay off,  I do not ever expect to win the first time I play any game. Two stars for being  fun until the levels get very hard to beat and seem stacked against you. If you are doing this to keep your mind sharper as you age, which I was, but find strategy does not help at all and it all seems like chance, then you might as well play something else.

author: WillChillsQ
title: Reviews must be fake
content: There is no way this has a 4.7 rating. The only points to this game is to get you to make purchases or watch ads. Many times you will play and exhaust all your moves. You will complete the entire game , except you have just one obstacle you have to complete. That forces you to either watch an ad, spend coins that they will happily sell to you, or start over. This happens countless times and there is no way you get to the end of the game that many times and only have one obstacle left. Even the boosters happen to fall just out of reach of helping you or point in the wrong direction of where they can help you. This game is more frustrating than entertaining and I’m sure the weak minded will spend money buying coins or boosters. To the developers, spare me the public relations response where you will “share my concerns” to make the game better. This is a money grab and there are many more games that are worthy of your time

author: J Ross2016
title: Great Game, But Lately…
content:
I’ve enjoyed this game for several years now, in my downtime; however, I’m a bit perturbed lately. I have several gripes, but the biggest one is with when I go to watch the ads to get the few bonus points…just as I’m only a few moves from winning the level. We’ll, the ads freeze and no matter how long I wait, all I get is a blank screen. I’d started noticing this once or twice earlier this year, though now, it’s occurring weekly. The only way to rectify has been to close the app and open it back again. At that point, I need to restart the level.
This could either be a problem with the app or an intentional push to have players purchase items in the app. Either way, please fix this issue or this loyal user will end up removing this app and no recommend Toon Blast to others. Also, my rating is strictly based on this issue. I’d gladly update if this gets resolved.

author: Jpmessiah
title: Lack of respect
content: During COVID, people are struggling to pay rent and yes, I get that game developers didn’t make this game not to make money, but to take advantage of people being home, scared and not going out, to try to make free-to-download games harder so that people spend more money than games that cost money to download is cruel. If I were to pay money to beat levels, I can easily see myself spending $20 a week or more. That adds up to more than the cost of a several console games. And then to not even respond to criticisms shows that these developers do not care. I really wish gamers would take a stand and stop throwing money to developers. As long as they do, game developers don’t care about those with little money to spend.

author: Bling Diggity
title: Addictive. And fun. But mostly addictive.
content:
Straightforward, simple, easy, and somewhat repetitive - so you'd think it would get boring quick right? WRONG. Once you get past level 20 it turns out it's not so simple or easy. Each level has a different strategy. The strategy that you used for one level to finish with 3 stars may not work at all on the next level. And no, the double-disco-ball mega explosions are not the answer to every level (just ask the clams/oysters). 
Admittedly this game has a few clones, and TBH it may very well be a clone itself of "Toy Blast" which I'm fairly certain came on the market first. But it doesn't matter. Toon Blast just has the right formula - the right mix of level difficulty, weapons, power-ups, team perks, etc - to be the best in it's category. And it is.

author: Phantom Ben

author: VolcanicPlayer
title: Make shop less expensive if you want people to pay
content:
I have enjoyed this game for a year or two until the big recent changes. I am a software developer and I have no problem with the developers wanting to earn money from this game. I’d like to support the developers by buying things from the shop, but I don’t because they are way too expensive.

So if you want to improve monetizing maybe give an update to the shop and see if that helps.

author: Stevecash83
title: How To Beat This Game
content:
Details on beating this game are at the bottom. Expand and see the last paragraph for information 

Hear me out, this is a well designed game and mostly enjoyable. However, as you’ll see on your own (or by reading reviews) this game is so blatantly greedy that if you actually want to “beat” the game, expect to spend a lot of money. Yes, the first hundred or so levels are achievable with strategy, but the later levels become increasingly more difficult and eventually painfully impossible. 

I’ve been strong enough to not spend a dime on in app purchases and in return I’ve been spending roughly a week stuck on a particular level until the game finally let me pass. One hundred coins can buy a new life, but 100 coins can take days to accumulate on your own, and even when using the extra lives it gives you only five more moves. Five! You’ll likely need about twenty more to get through, and if you were paying for those lives you’d have to refinance your home to do so.

If you want the best experience from this game, join a team, help other players get lives, play on until you reach level 200 and then exit the game, hold your finger over the game’s icon, and press the little ‘x’ in the corner. Then press “yes” on the prompt that asks “are you sure you want to delete this app?”.  Using this method is the quickest way to beat the game.

Enjoy!

author: Varnished Truth
title: Totally Rigged Game
content: First and foremost, this game wants you to spend money. At times it lets you have easy success. At other times it gets really difficult hoping you will spend money to win. As you gain experience playing the game, you will notice how it is rigged to get you to pay up. It gets increasingly frustrating over time and that is the plan. Fork over some money or deal with loads of frustration. The fun slowly evaporates until you delete the app. Here’s an example. After you earn a magic disco ball, the game eventually starts trying to take it from you by forcing you to use all of your boosters and loot to keep from losing it. When you have used them up your only recourse is to pay up or lose the disco ball. It gets you to watch OBNOXIOUS advertisements to get extra moves. Sometimes when you click to watch an advertisement, it says ‘ad not ready’ and it will not allow you to continue that puzzle. Wow! Rigged, greedy and unfair.

author: Judipotts
title: Fix the free minutes
content:
This game is the best, especially if you are competitive and earn enough points to join a team and get into tournaments. **Note to producers: The only fix that I would recommend is to allow players to bank their “free minutes” In this day and age most people run on a tight schedule and to earn free minutes is worthless if you cannot use them immediately.
Added note:  I wish the people at toon blast who keep tabs on the game would not kick my connection error on during every single tournament that I play in.   When I put in a request for the issue to the creators, I am always told it’s a Wi-Fi problem and it is not because no matter what Wi-Fi am I connected to the same problem occurs and it only happens during tournaments which leads me to believe that it is the creators that are doing it.  And that is not fair gaming.  So in other words, the game is rigged in my opinion.

author: CircusCone
title: Plays on a Stress and Frustration Fueled Cycle
content: The game is a great time waster, but is obviously designed to create long win streaks and then pull it out from under you and make you claw your way out of difficult levels.  You can get in long streaks that give you bonuses to help you beat progressively more levels, but then out of nowhere you’ll find a level that is specifically designed to be difficult for the random nature of the game and you lose it all.  This is especially frustrating because since it’s random, you truly have little agency over you beat or lose a level.  Now don’t get me wrong, there’s some strategies that work, but other times it just all collapses and you have no options.  When you get in those levels, there’s no feeling of accomplishment when you beat them, just frustration that it happened and now you have to build everything up again.

author: completely_undone_86
title: Deeper than it looks
content: Don’t let the cartoony stuff throw you; this is a sophisticated strategy game that actually reminds me of chess. As you get deeper into the game you will find yourself planning three and four moves in advance (and thankfully there is no time limit a la Candy Crush with its bombs). You will also discover that the most powerful tools are not always the correct ones, and that finesse trumps strength. I also want to mention that the game rewards skillful cheapskates; I’ve only bought add-ons once and I am over level 300. (Sorry, developers!) The community mini-challenges are fun and add zest. I only wish I could play certain levels over again - level 280 was especially fun. Smart as Sudoku, as visually fun as Candy Crush, goofy and engaging.

author: silentshowers
title: One of the best games out there for phone
content:
Im a gamer, but I’m not really into phone games. Not my thing. I play this on and off from time to time though. I don’t really write reviews either, but this game is worth the time. I also like to code/program for fun and am somewhat beginner-intermediate level. author: Crys345
title: You will become addicted without even realizing it!
content: I love this game! It’s so easy to beat the levels and I only play for about 30 minutes total per day. I initially played maybe 2-3 times per week for like 15 minutes per day. Then, I joined a team that was serious about helps and the team score, and the next thing I know, I’m opening the game every lunch break just to send help/lives (I play at night to detox). The lives really come in handy, and my team always wins the tournaments and team chests so I’ve never had to buy the booster packages. (I’m in Champions League btw, which is the highest level for the game until the developers create new ones.) Moral of the story: Join a good team, and you’ll fall in love with the game and maybe meet a few decent people along the way.

author: CWilb
title: Great Game in Lower Levels
content:
Beating a level is like playing a slot machine. It’s really up to the game whether you’ll win or lose. And just like a slot machine, you’ll eventually win if you play long enough. The problem is, when you get to the higher levels, you have to play the same level over and over so many times before advancing that it gets boring. I’ve asked support to reset my account so I can start at level 1, a couple of times. They’ve done it, although this last time I had to really fight for it. I’d love to see the option a built-in feature. 

I’m sure the concern is that no one will buy boosters if it’s too easy, but there are daily challenges & competitions that motivate those purchases. And customers aren’t leaving for a game that’s not impossible to beat.

author: SCREENWRITER09
title: 10 out of 10 game from someone who’s played just about every puzzle game
content: Probably one of the best puzzle games I’ve ever played it’s basically one of the best if you’re just into doing puzzles this is for you it has its own unique flair that makes it special no ads and it works in no WiFi zones trust me it’s better than royal kingdom recently it’s added on those cheap little save Bruno things like Homescapes and royal kingdom has but this game doesn’t even need that if you’re looking for a fun easy and relaxing puzzle game this is it I’ve been playing it for years which shows you even when I was a kid I played it it’s pretty easy just enjoyable sometimes you don’t need all that extra junk just a good block puzzle

author: Starlet42
title: It’s fun. No ads ever. Free. Join a team!
content: Why do people think that you’re taking lives from others? The lives are free when you’re on a team and you get coins for helping. If you play your timing right you could start out with 15 lives with no cost to anyone. You don’t give up anything. You’re not taking away anything. You receive a coin for every life you give.  If you wait 2 1/2 hours you get five lives back Plus whatever lives were given you in Helps. Each life you click help to give gives you a coin. I think it’s fun. It’s free! There are NO ADS.  I have spent money on lazy days. Remember when you’d drop $10 at an arcade easy? That’s how I look at it. Once a month I’ll drop $7 for some extra help. Love the tournies. Love the chance to get more coins every day.

author: Trump is your Prez
title: The game had turned into an endless demand for money
content:
This game has changed over the years but in recent times it’s just turned into a money grab. You will get stuck on levels where you will get stuck for 3, 4, 5 days trying hundreds of times to get past a single level. Or, you can spend a $1.99 to get as many 35 “extra” moves for that one single level. Then, you might get a few “easier” levels which might take only a few tries, or 30 and then you are right back to a near-impossible level where you are stuck. 
I am currently stuck on a level that I’ve probably tried 400 times to win. No thanks. I’m tired of paying endlessly now that they’ve formulated the game to basically force you to pay to move on. I refuse to pay another dime until they back off of the greed factor. That will probably never happen so I’m simply going to back off from playing it so much and find something else to do with my time.

author: Alpendirndl
title: Frustrating once you get to champion level
content: I have played this game for several years now, and even invested some money into it. After all this time, I had finally reached the champion level. That’s when my frustration started. First the champion level started at 5800. Now, a few month later it has gone up to 6250. What is so frustrating is that you lets say you reach the champion level needed of 6200 on Monday. Now you play all week and reach maybe 50 or 100 stages. However once you are there, your levels will remain the same and instead of level you will collect stages. Come next Monday, they are raising the champion level by 50. One would think all of the stages would convert to levels and you just need to add on, but no! You stages disappear and you are back to 6200, your champion status is void and you start from the beginning. All of the time, effort, and money you have put in the week before have disappeared very frustrating!

author: Bayprodigy707
title: Fun game, but!
content: This is a great game to pass the time, and it holds its own compared to other app based games. My only problem is sometimes they make to stages so difficult to pass. Yes challenges are great but it clears this game is out to get your money and yes I’ve spent some money. Honestly it seems like this game monitors your game play and spending. To me, it seems the game keeps track of pay schedules and around pay day the stages get harder. The bait is up until pay day I’m blazing through stages and it builds anxiety that makes you want to keep playing no matter the cost. As soon as the pay week rolls around,  boom no more winning. The worst is when you created a momentum and you got your crown all the way out in the game gives you power ups dinner level comes up where it doesn’t matter your momentum you get no power rubs in this one of the hardest levels to beat. Download at your own risk.

author: Mom of four kids
title: Haven’t spent a penny
content:
With the daily bonus, extra lives from teammates, and perseverance, it is possible to get to the upper levels without spending money. Might have to play a level 20 times, but each play you learn a little more about how to clear it. It makes that last play, when you clear a level youv’e been stuck on, all that much sweeter. I play with the assumption that every level is beatable without spending money and it hasn’t let me down yet. 
I regularly exceed the available levels (and play the non-themed levels for a few days every couple of weeks). But I have also been known to play a level for a day or more, learning a bit more each time, and getting excited when that little bit of luck, finally, gets me through.

author: GrapMI
title: Times Have Changed
content: This was once my favorite game but over the years things have gone down the drain. There is a lot of cheating, game crashes when you have one more move left to win, rockets slowing down to miss blocks or going through them without affecting them, etc. When you reach out to support, with or without proof, the issues are blamed on your WiFi or they don’t see an issue at all. I’ve contacted them 4 times in the last month or two and never got anything other than generic answers or told to connect to stable WiFi. This the only game I seem to have issues with. I’m over it and I would advise you not to download the game and if you do, don’t spend a dime to play.

author: design goddess
title: Don’t let your kids play this game
content: After every single game it asks to connect to your Facebook page. Every. Single. Time. You’d think not picking that option once would be enough. I could see that being tempting to a kid after awhile. If you allow/use in app purchases this game will empty your wallet. The split second a game ends a huge button pops up asking to spend coins to continue the game. Even when there is no hope of winning the game. It’s very easy to accidentally hit that button.  That will take all the coins earned/purchased in just a few moves. You can also buy boosters. Guaranteed that the only way to win some games is the booster you don’t have. I can see how this game would be addicting, I can also see how someone might spend money they don’t intend to or pair it with Facebook just to stop the pop up. It’s been designed to get your Facebook and/or money. This game is just a flash in a pan. Almost everyone I know who played this game has stopped because of these problems.

title: Fun — till it isn’t.
content: This is a game that tries to hook you before you reach the stage where to be able to advance you have to buy additional powers.  I decided I would not do that and see how far I could get.  I am up to level 284, not as far as other like minded commenters got, but then I am not much of a game player.  The game is fun to play.  At lower levels when you are having particular difficulty getting past one level, you feel that some expenditure may be worth it to get past and so you can get to some others at which you may win.  But then you get to a point of increased difficulty where you’re pretty sure that you don’t have much of a chance of solving any higher level without paying.  Then, unless you’re made of the stuff, you figure what’s the use.  That’s where I am.  It’s no longer fun — the cynicism and rapacity of the creators are all too clear and the only question is how much of a sucker I am.  Time to pull the plug.
